_comment: One source of truth for the technique library (/library/) and the labels on every form page. Keys are the `tech` and `stance` values used in forms/*.json. Slugs are the URL anchors (/library/<family>/#<slug>) and must never change once published. Descriptions are our own words.

stances.title: Stances
stances.intro: Where the feet go and where the weight sits. Every move in a poomsae starts from one of these, so they are worth learning before any technique. The footprint beside each stance is the same top-down glyph used on the form pages: red foot leads, the blue tick is the way you face.

blocks.title: Blocks
blocks.intro: Blocks meet an attack with the forearm or the hand and turn it aside. The name says the height (arae low, momtong middle, eolgul high) and often the direction the arm travels (an inward, bakkat outward).

strikes.title: Strikes
strikes.intro: Jireugi is a straight punch, chigi a swinging strike, jjireugi a thrust with the fingertips. Grabs and breaks are listed here too.

kicks.title: Kicks
kicks.intro: Every kick in the Taegeuk and early black-belt forms, with the part of the foot that makes contact. In the diagrams a kick and the strike after it share one number: 8-1 is the kick, 8-2 the landing technique.

hands-feet.title: Hands and feet
hands-feet.intro: The striking and blocking surfaces. Every technique in the library names the surface it uses and links here, so you can see exactly which part of the hand, arm or foot does the work.

jumeok.name: Jumeok
jumeok.desc: The flat front of the closed fist, striking with the first two knuckles. The wrist stays straight so the forearm lines up behind them.

deung-jumeok.name: Deung jumeok
deung-jumeok.desc: The back of the closed fist, again the first two knuckles, used in a snapping strike to the face.

me-jumeok.name: Me jumeok
me-jumeok.desc: The fleshy little-finger side of the closed fist, swung like a hammer.

sonnal.name: Sonnal
sonnal.desc: The outer edge of the open hand, from the base of the little finger to the wrist. Fingers held together and firm, thumb bent in.

pyeonsonkkeut.name: Pyeonsonkkeut
pyeonsonkkeut.desc: The tips of the flat, straight fingers, with the middle finger slightly bent so the three tips line up.

batangson.name: Batangson
batangson.desc: The heel of the palm, fingers bent back slightly out of the way.

agwison.name: Agwison
agwison.desc: The curve between the thumb and the index finger, hand spread into a C, used against the throat.

bam-jumeok.name: Bam jumeok
bam-jumeok.desc: A fist with the middle finger's second knuckle pushed out ahead of the others, concentrating the strike on one point.

sonnal-deung.name: Sonnal deung
sonnal-deung.desc: The thumb-side edge of the open hand, from the base of the index finger to the wrist, with the thumb folded under the palm.

sondung.name: Sondung
sondung.desc: The back of the open hand, used for downward and side strikes.

sonbadak.name: Sonbadak
sonbadak.desc: The whole flat of the open hand, fingers together, used to push, press, grab or brace.

palkup.name: Palkup
palkup.desc: The point and the forearm side of the bent elbow, for strikes at close range.

palmok.name: Palmok
palmok.desc: The lower forearm near the wrist, the blocking surface for most fist blocks. Kukkiwon names the edge used: bakkat palmok (the outer, little-finger side) or an palmok (the inner, thumb side).

mureup.name: Mureup
mureup.desc: The top of the bent knee, driven upward at close range.

apchuk.name: Apchuk
apchuk.desc: The pad under the toes, with the toes pulled back out of the way. The contact point for front and roundhouse kicks.

balnal.name: Balnal
balnal.desc: The outer edge of the foot, heel side, with the foot flexed. The contact point for the side kick.

balbadak.name: Balbadak
balbadak.desc: The flat underside of the foot, used to slap a target such as your own open palm.

dwitkumchi.name: Dwitkumchi
dwitkumchi.desc: The back of the heel, driven straight back in the back piercing kick.

ready.name: Naranhi seogi
ready.desc: Feet parallel, one foot-width apart, legs straight and weight even. The stance for gibon junbi at the start and end of a form.
points: Toes point straight ahead
Knees soft, not locked

close.name: Moa seogi
close.desc: Feet together, inside edges touching, legs straight.
points: Weight even on both feet
Stand tall: chin in, shoulders down

walk.name: Ap seogi
walk.desc: One natural walking step. Both legs straight, weight even, the feet almost in line with each other.
points: Step length about one stride
Rear foot may turn out slightly
Hips and shoulders face forward

front.name: Ap kubi
front.desc: A long, low stance. About one and a half steps long and one fist wide, the front knee bent over the toes and the rear leg straight.
points: Front shin near vertical, knee over the ball of the foot
Rear leg straight, heel down, foot turned out about 30°
Most of the weight on the front leg

back.name: Dwit kubi
back.desc: Heels in line in an L shape: the front foot points forward, the rear foot turns out 90°. Both knees bend and most of the weight sits on the rear leg. Our chips and instructions name it by the front foot: "L · Dwit kubi" is the left foot forward.
points: Rear knee bent and pushed out over the rear toes
Hips and chest turn to the side, not square to the front foot
Front foot light, ready to kick

tiger.name: Beom seogi
tiger.desc: A short stance with almost all the weight on the bent rear leg. The front foot rests on its ball, heel raised, about one foot-length ahead.
points: Front knee bent and turned slightly in
Body upright, sitting on the rear leg

nieun.name: Nieunja seogi
nieun.desc: The feet stand at right angles to each other, like the letter ㄴ, heels about one foot-length apart, knees slightly bent and the weight spread evenly. A short, mobile stance between steps.
points: Front foot points forward, rear foot turned 90°
Shorter than a back stance; weight on both legs

gyeot.name: Gyeotdari seogi
gyeot.desc: The front knee bends over the front foot while the rear foot comes in close behind and beside the front heel, only its ball on the floor, the rear knee bent in behind the front knee as if supporting it.
points: Rear knee tucked in behind the front knee
Weight mostly on the front leg

ogeum.name: Ogeum seogi
ogeum.desc: Like crane stance, standing on one bent leg, but the instep of the lifted foot presses into the back of the standing knee instead of its side.
points: Standing knee bent, weight centred over the foot
Lifted foot hooked behind the knee

fixed.name: Gojung sogi
fixed.desc: An ITF stance, first met in Won-Hyo. Shaped like the L-stance but a little longer, with the weight shared evenly between the legs and the body half-facing. Named by the front foot: a left fixed stance has the left foot forward. Drawn here with the L-stance figure.
points: Both knees bent, weight even
Front foot points forward, rear foot turned out

vertical.name: Soojik sogi
vertical.desc: An ITF stance, first met in Hwa-Rang. A short L shape, about one shoulder width from heel to heel, with both legs straight and a little more of the weight on the rear leg. Named by the rear foot, like the L-stance: a left vertical stance has the left foot back. Drawn here with the L-stance figure.
points: Both legs straight
Front foot points forward, rear foot turned out about 90°
Slightly more weight on the rear leg

oneleg.name: Waebal sogi
oneleg.desc: An ITF stance, first met in Po-Eun. Stand on one leg, the knee slightly bent, with the other foot drawn up beside the standing knee joint, ready to kick. Named by the standing leg. Drawn here with the crane stance figure.
points: Standing knee slightly bent
Lifted foot beside the standing knee joint

lowst.name: Nachuo sogi
lowst.desc: An ITF stance, first met in Joong-Gun. A walking stance made longer and lower, the front knee bent well forward. Named by the front foot. Drawn here with the walking-stance figure.
points: Longer than the walking stance by about a foot
Front knee well bent, rear leg straight

horse.name: Juchum seogi
horse.desc: Feet parallel and about two foot-lengths apart, knees bent and pushed outward, weight even, back upright.
points: Knees over the toes, not collapsing inward
Back straight, weight even on both feet

cross.name: Kkoa seogi
cross.desc: One foot crossed behind the other, resting on its ball next to the front foot. In the forms it usually follows a jump.
points: Weight on the front foot
Knees bent together

crane.name: Hakdari seogi
crane.desc: Stand on one slightly bent leg; the other foot rests its inside edge against the standing knee. Named for the standing leg.
points: Lifted knee turned out to the side
Balance over the standing foot

junbi.name: Junbi
junbi.desc: Gibon junbi: in parallel stance, both fists in front of the belt, a fist-width from the body. Every form starts and ends here.

tongmil.name: Tongmilgi junbi
tongmil.desc: The ready posture of Koryo: the open hands rise slowly to the chest and push forward to face height, fingertips angled toward each other, as if pushing a rock.

cover.name: Bojumeok
cover.desc: One fist wrapped in the other open hand and raised slowly in front of the chest, feet together. A moment of stillness in Taegeuk Chil Jang.

gyeopson.name: Gyeopson junbi
gyeopson.desc: The ready posture of Pyongwon: in closed stance, the open hands rest one over the other in front of the lower belly, left over right, and the breath settles before the form begins.

low.name: Arae makki
low.desc: The blocking fist starts at the opposite shoulder and sweeps down across the body, stopping a fist above the front thigh. Clears a kick or low punch.

alow.name: Geodeureo arae makki
alow.desc: A low block with the other fist supporting it just behind the blocking forearm, for a stronger block.

inside.name: Momtong an makki
inside.desc: The forearm swings from outside the body to the centre line at chest height, forearm upright, turning a middle attack across the body.

outer.name: Momtong bakkat makki
outer.desc: The forearm swings from inside to outside at shoulder height, the fist level with the shoulder, turning a middle attack away from the body.

aouter.name: Geodeureo momtong bakkat makki
aouter.desc: An outer middle block with the other fist supporting it under the blocking elbow.

high.name: Eolgul makki
high.desc: The forearm rises across the front of the face and stops a fist above the forehead, angled so a strike from above slides off.

houter.name: Eolgul bakkat makki
houter.desc: An outer block at face height: the forearm turns out with the fist level with the eyes.

ahside.name: Eolgul geodeureo yeop makki
ahside.desc: In horse stance, one forearm rises to the side at head height, elbow bent, while the other fist lies across the chest to brace it.

wedge.name: Momtong hecho makki
wedge.desc: Both forearms cross in front of the chest and open outward together, wedging apart a two-handed attack.

spread.name: Arae hecho makki
spread.desc: Both fists cross in front of the body and sweep down and out to each side at once.

xlow.name: Eotgeoreo arae makki
xlow.desc: Both fists drive down and cross at the wrists in front of the lower belly, trapping a low kick in the X.

scissors.name: Gawi makki
scissors.desc: Two blocks at once: one arm makes an outer middle block while the other makes a low block, the arms passing like the blades of scissors.

mountain.name: Oesanteul makki
mountain.desc: One arm makes a high outer block while the other makes a low block to the opposite side, the shape of a single mountain peak.

santeul.name: Santeul makki
santeul.desc: Both arms make high outer blocks to each side, elbows bent at right angles: the 山 shape that gives Keumgang its floor line.

hsanteul.name: Hecho taesan makki
hsanteul.desc: Both forearms open out and up to each side at head height, elbows bent, as the foot lands in horse stance: a wide, mountain-shaped block.

keumgang.name: Keumgang makki
keumgang.desc: A high block and a low block made together, one arm up and one down. In Keumgang it is held on one leg in crane stance.

kmomtong.name: Keumgang momtong makki
kmomtong.desc: A middle block and a high block made together, one arm at the chest and one above the head.

ksout.name: Hansonnal bakkat makki
ksout.desc: A single open hand swings out at shoulder height, blocking with the knife edge, the other fist at the hip.

ksblock.name: Sonnal momtong makki
ksblock.desc: One knife hand blocks outward at shoulder height while the other open hand guards the solar plexus, palm up. Usually made in back stance.

ksin.name: Hansonnal momtong an makki
ksin.desc: The open hand swings inward to the centre line at chest height, blocking with the knife edge.

kslow.name: Sonnal arae makki
kslow.desc: A low block made with the knife edge of the open hand.

kslowa.name: Sonnal geodeureo naeryeo makki
kslowa.desc: A low knife-hand block driven down over the front leg, with the other open hand held palm up across the body to back it up.

ksside.name: Hansonnal yeop makki
ksside.desc: In horse stance, the knife hand blocks out to the side at shoulder height while the body faces forward.

kspread.name: Sonnal arae hecho makki
kspread.desc: Both knife hands cross in front of the body and sweep down and out to each side.

twist.name: Hansonnal eolgul bitureo makki
twist.desc: The knife hand blocks at face height with the hand turned so the palm faces out, the arm crossing the body's centre line.

palm.name: Batangson momtong an makki
palm.desc: The palm heel swings inward to the centre line at chest height, pushing a middle attack aside.

apalm.name: Geodeureo batangson momtong an makki
apalm.desc: A palm inside block with the other fist supporting it under the blocking elbow.

pressdown.name: Batangson nulleo makki
pressdown.desc: The open palm presses straight down in front of the body, pushing an attack down and away.

khinge.name: Keun doljjeogwi
khinge.desc: In horse stance, one elbow drives out to the side while the other fist pulls across the chest, both forearms level: the arms swing like a door hinge.

shinge.name: Jageun doljjeogwi
shinge.desc: Both fists stacked at one hip, one on top of the other, as the body turns: a compact preparation in Taebaek and Jitae, made in crane stance (in Jitae also before the diamond punch).

punch.name: Momtong jireugi
punch.desc: A straight punch to the solar plexus. The fist turns palm-down as it lands while the other fist pulls back to the hip. Called bandae when the punching hand matches the front foot, baro when it is the opposite hand.

hpunch.name: Eolgul jireugi
hpunch.desc: A straight punch to the face, aimed at the philtrum, the space between the nose and the upper lip.

sidepunch.name: Yeop jireugi
sidepunch.desc: In horse stance, a straight punch out to the side while the body faces forward.

tpunch.name: Pyojeok jireugi
tpunch.desc: One hand opens as a target out to the side; the other fist punches across the body into it.

uppercut.name: Dangkyeo teok jireugi
uppercut.desc: One hand pulls the opponent in while the other fist drives up under the jaw, palm toward you.

duppercut.name: Dujumeok jeocho jireugi
duppercut.desc: Both fists punch upward together from the hips, palms up, to the opponent's body.

backfist.name: Deung jumeok ap chigi
backfist.desc: The fist swings up and forward from the opposite shoulder, striking the face with the back of the knuckles.

stompbf.name: Jitjjigi · danggyeo deung jumeok ap chigi
stompbf.desc: One foot stamps down in horse stance while the back of the fist strikes out to the side at face height; the other hand grabs and pulls back to the hip as it lands.

abackfist.name: Geodeureo deung jumeok ap chigi
abackfist.desc: A back-fist strike at face height with the other arm brought across under it for support.

obackfist.name: Deung jumeok bakkat chigi
obackfist.desc: A back-fist that swings outward across the body to the side of the head.

hammer.name: Mejumeok naeryeo chigi
hammer.desc: The fist swings in a big arc over the head and down, striking with the little-finger side.

hammerlow.name: Mejumeok arae pyojeok chigi
hammerlow.desc: Both hands rise overhead and circle out and down slowly; the hammer fist strikes into the other open palm in front of the belly. The closing gesture of Koryo.

neck.name: Sonnal mok chigi
neck.desc: The knife hand swings inward to the side of the neck, palm up, the other fist at the hip.

jebi.name: Jebipoom mok chigi
jebi.desc: One knife hand blocks high while the other strikes the neck at the same moment, the arms spread like a swallow's wings.

ksstrike.name: Hansonnal bakkat chigi
ksstrike.desc: The knife hand swings outward from the opposite shoulder to the side of the neck, palm down.

spear.name: Pyeonsonkkeut sewo jjireugi
spear.desc: The open hand, held upright with the thumb on top, thrusts straight to the solar plexus. The other hand presses down under the striking elbow.

lspear.name: Pyeonsonkkeut jeocho jjireugi
lspear.desc: A spear hand thrust low with the palm turned up, while the other fist pulls to the opposite shoulder.

palmjaw.name: Batangson teok chigi
palmjaw.desc: The palm heel drives up and forward into the jaw.

arc.name: Kaljaebi
arc.desc: The hand opens into an arc between thumb and index finger and drives into the throat.

elbow.name: Palkup dollyeo chigi
elbow.desc: The bent elbow swings round horizontally to the side of the jaw.

upelbow.name: Palkup ollyeo chigi
upelbow.desc: The elbow drives up and forward under an opponent's chin, the fist finishing beside the ear and the hips turning in behind it.

eltarget.name: Palkup pyojeok chigi
eltarget.desc: The elbow swings round into the other open palm, held as a target in front of the body.

sideelbow.name: Palkup yeop chigi
sideelbow.desc: In horse stance, the elbow drives straight out to the side while the other palm pushes against the striking fist.

yoke.name: Meongye chigi
yoke.desc: Both elbows drive out to the sides at once, fists in front of the chest, like the yoke across an ox's shoulders. In Pyongwon it is made in a cross stance, looking along the line; in Sipjin in a horse stance.

hwangso.name: Hwangso makki
hwangso.desc: Both fists rise slowly from the belt past the chest and stop above the forehead, a little apart, forearms angled like the horns of an ox. Sipjin opens with it; in Jitae it is made in horse stance, the fists rising straight up about hip width apart. Over about five seconds.

pouter.name: Sonbadak geodeureo momtong bakkat makki
pouter.desc: An outer block with the inner forearm while the other hand, open, presses its palm against the inside of the blocking wrist to brace it.

wristturn.name: Palmok dollyeo
wristturn.desc: Held where the outer block finished, the blocking hand opens slowly and the wrist rolls over, palm down, as if loosening and then turning a grip on the forearm. About five seconds.

hspear.name: Pyeonsonkkeut eopeo jjireugi
hspear.desc: A spear-hand thrust with the palm facing down and the fingers level, driven straight to the solar plexus.

pgrab.name: Pyojeok japgi
pgrab.desc: As the feet cross, the leading hand reaches across the body and closes on a target, an arm or a collar, ready to pull it onto the punch that follows.

dsidepunch.name: Danggyeo yeop jireugi
dsidepunch.desc: The grabbing hand pulls back to the hip while the other fist punches straight out to the side, over the leading leg of a horse stance.

rockpush.name: Bawi milgi
rockpush.desc: Both open hands gather at one hip, then push forward and up together, one at head height and one in front of the face, as if rolling a heavy boulder away. Done slowly, over about five seconds.

rdwedge.name: Sonnal deung momtong hecho makki
rdwedge.desc: The forearms cross in front of the chest and open out to both sides at chest height, blocking with the ridge of each open hand.

lift.name: Geodeo olligi
lift.desc: The leading arm scoops low and lifts up in front of the body, catching an incoming leg on the forearm and open hand and raising it to tip the attacker off balance.

chetdari.name: Chetdari jireugi
chetdari.desc: Both fists punch forward together at solar-plexus height, forearms parallel and about two fists apart, like the two rails of a sieve frame (chetdari).

ksxlow.name: Sonnal eotgeoreo arae makki
ksxlow.desc: Both open hands drive down and cross at the wrists in front of the lower belly, catching a low attack in the X between the knife-hands.

rdblock.name: Sonnal deung momtong makki
rdblock.desc: The open hand swings out to block at chest height with its ridge, the thumb side, while the other open hand guards in front of the chest.

anouter.name: An palmok momtong bakkat makki
anouter.desc: An outer middle block made with the inner (thumb-side) edge of the forearm: the fist starts low by the opposite hip and the arm swings up and out, stopping at shoulder height.

ksrise.name: Sonnal ollyeo makki
ksrise.desc: A single knife hand rises across the front of the face and stops above the forehead, like an upward block made with the open hand.

kpunch.name: Keumgang ap jireugi
kpunch.desc: An upward block and a middle punch made at the same moment, one arm rising above the head while the other fist drives forward. Both fists start palm up.

ainside.name: Geodeureo momtong an makki
ainside.desc: An inside middle block with the other fist brought under the blocking elbow to back it up.

lowside.name: Naeryeo yeop makki
lowside.desc: The forearm sweeps down and out to the side of the body, turning away a low attack from that side. Jitae makes it in horse stance and in crane stance.

hammertgt.name: Mejumeok pyojeok an chigi
hammertgt.desc: One hand opens out to the side as a target at face height; the other hammer fist swings in across the body and strikes into it, the trunk and the elbow turning together.

nalgae.name: Nalgae pyeogi
nalgae.desc: From overlapped hands, both palms rise to the chest and push slowly out to the sides at shoulder height, wrists bent back, like a bird opening its wings. It gathers power and splits an opponent's force both ways.

kshopen.name: Sonnal eolgul hecho makki
kshopen.desc: Both open hands rise in front of the body past the face and spread apart above the head, edges outward, opening an attack from above.

bamupper.name: Bam jumeok ollyeo jireugi
bamupper.desc: Both extended-knuckle fists drive upward together from the waist, under the jaw, ending about lip height.

kstwist.name: Sonnal biteureo makki
kstwist.desc: The knife hand meets the attacking wrist and turns over as it blocks, ready to take hold of it.

wristout.name: Bakkat teureo ppaegi
wristout.desc: The held hand twists outward and draws back toward the body, slowly, freeing the wrist or pulling the opponent in.

aanouter.name: Geodeureo an palmok momtong bakkat makki
aanouter.desc: An inner-forearm outer middle block with the other fist supporting it under the blocking elbow.

hwidul.name: Hwidulleo makki
hwidul.desc: The blocking arm swings in a big circle, down, up and out, sweeping the attack aside before the fist comes back to the hip for a punch.

swingpull.name: Hwidulleo jaba danggigi
swingpull.desc: The swinging-block circle made with an open hand, which takes hold at the end and pulls the opponent in toward the next punch.

twouter.name: An palmok biteureo bakkat makki
twouter.desc: An outer block with the rear arm, using the inner forearm and turning the trunk the other way, so the block ends at the edge of the shoulder line.

outpress.name: An palmok bakkat makki · batangson nulleo makki
outpress.desc: A short inner-forearm outer block while the other palm slaps onto the blocking wrist and presses down, made on the first of Cheonkwon's quick steps.

kside.name: Keumgang yeop jireugi
kside.desc: In horse stance, one arm makes an upward block while the other fist punches out to the side, both at once.

dtkick.name: Dolgae pyojeok an chagi
dtkick.desc: A jump with a full turn in the air; before landing, the kicking leg swings inward into your own open hand held out as a target.

pmountain.name: Pyeonson oesan makki
pmountain.desc: A single mountain block made with open hands: the knife hand blocks down over the front leg while the other hand blocks high and out with its ridge. Slowly, about five seconds.

taesan.name: Taesan milgi
taesan.desc: Both open hands push forward together, one with its fingertips at belt height and the other at lip height, as if moving a great mountain. Slowly, with the whole body tensed, about five seconds.

dhammerin.name: Du mejumeok an chigi
dhammerin.desc: Both fists swing out and up to about lip height, then drive inward together with the hammer fists, ending level with the edges of the body at chest height.

presarc.name: Nulleo makki · ageumson geodeureo ap chigi
presarc.desc: One palm presses an attack down while the other hand strikes forward to the throat with the arc between thumb and forefinger, stepping in on the diagonal.

lowtgt.name: An palmok pyojeok arae makki
lowtgt.desc: The blocking arm drops from shoulder height, thumb down, and the inner forearm meets the other open palm held as a target at belt height.

kskeumgang.name: Sonnal keumgang makki
kskeumgang.desc: A diamond block made with open hands: one knife hand blocks high above the head while the other blocks low.

stompbf2.name: Jitjjigi · deung jumeok ap chigi
stompbf2.desc: The kicking foot stamps down in front and the other foot crosses in behind; the back fist strikes forward to the face as the foot lands.

presspear.name: Nulleo makki · pyeonsonkkeut sewo jjireugi
presspear.desc: Landing from a jump onto one leg, one palm presses an attack down while the other hand thrusts forward with the fingertips, hand upright. Ilyeo shouts on it.

oesanskick.name: Oesan yeop chagi
oesanskick.en: Side kick with single mountain block
oesanskick.desc: A slow side kick made together with a single mountain block, one arm low over the kicking leg and the other high; the block and the kick finish at the same moment. About five seconds.

xhigh.name: Eotgeoreo eolgul makki
xhigh.desc: Both forearms rise and cross at the wrists above the forehead, catching an attack from above in the fork.

twgrab.name: Du son pyeo biteureo jaba danggigi
twgrab.desc: From the high X block the hands open, turn over until the wrists change places, take hold and pull the opponent down toward the next punch.

hipready.name: Dujumeok heori junbi
hipready.desc: Feet together, both fists drawn straight to the waist, a little slower than a normal move, before kicking.

jskick.name: Twimyeo yeop chagi
jskick.desc: Straight after a front kick, the body springs into the air and the other leg drives out in a side kick.

anpalmok.name: Anpalmok kaunde yop makgi
anpalmok.desc: An ITF block, first met in Chon-Ji. In L-stance with the body half-turned, the forearm swings out from across the body and stops at shoulder height, the inner (thumb-side) forearm meeting the attack, the other fist pulling back to the hip.

sangpalmok.name: Sang palmok makgi
sangpalmok.desc: An ITF block, first met in Dan-Gun. Both forearms block at once: the front arm blocks to the side at shoulder height while the rear arm rises to guard above the forehead. Done in L-stance.

kssidestrike.name: Sonkal kaunde yop taerigi
kssidestrike.desc: An ITF strike, first met at the end of Do-San. In sitting stance facing forward, the knife-hand swings out to the side and strikes at shoulder height, arm almost straight, the other fist pulled back to the hip.

moajunbia.desc: An ITF ready posture, first met in Won-Hyo. Feet together; the left hand wraps the right fist, held in front of the body.
moajunbia.name: Moa junbi sogi A

guburyoa.desc: An ITF ready posture for a side kick, first met in Won-Hyo. Stand on one bent leg with the other foot lifted beside its knee, side-on to the target, the arms held in a forearm guarding block.
guburyoa.name: Guburyo junbi sogi A

lowkick.desc: An ITF kick. A front snap kick aimed low, the ball of the foot snapping out and back.
lowkick.name: Najunde apcha busigi

circular.desc: An ITF block, first met in Won-Hyo. The inner forearm sweeps round in a circle, low to high across the body, and finishes upright in front of the shoulder, turning the attack aside.
circular.name: Anpalmok dollimyo makgi

fguard.desc: An ITF block done in L-stance: the front forearm blocks to the front at shoulder height while the rear fist guards in front of the solar plexus.
fguard.name: Palmok kaunde daebi makgi

sitext.desc: Not a strike: in Yul-Gok the student settles into sitting stance and extends one fist straight out to the front at shoulder height, measuring the distance for the punches that follow.
sitext.name: Annun sogi

golcho.desc: An ITF block, first met in Yul-Gok. The open palm hooks in from the side at chest height, catching the attacking arm and drawing it in; two in a row (one each hand) set up the punch.
golcho.name: Sonbadak kaunde golcho makgi

sangsonkal.desc: An ITF block, first met in Yul-Gok. Like the twin forearm block but with open hands: in L-stance the front knife-hand blocks to the side at shoulder height while the rear knife-hand rises to guard above the forehead.
sangsonkal.name: Sang sonkal makgi

doopalmok.desc: An ITF block: a high block made with one forearm while the other fist braces it near the elbow, the two arms working together.
doopalmok.name: Doo palmok nopunde makgi

moajunbib.desc: An ITF ready posture, first met in Joong-Gun. Feet together; the left hand wraps the right fist, held lower than in ready stance A, in front of the abdomen.
moajunbib.name: Moa junbi sogi B

yobapcha.desc: An ITF kick, first met in Joong-Gun. From L-stance the front foot snaps out low to the side-front with the ball of the foot, the hands held where they were.
yobapcha.name: Najunde yobap cha busigi

ollyo.desc: An ITF block, first met in Joong-Gun. In rear foot stance the open palm rises from below in front of the body, lifting an attack upward.
ollyo.name: Sonbadak ollyo makgi

twinvert.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Joong-Gun. Both fists punch together at eye level, held vertical with the thumbs up, shoulder-width apart.
twinvert.name: Sang joomuk nopunde sewo jirugi

jappyosul.desc: An ITF movement, met in Do-San and Joong-Gun: twisting the held arm and slipping forward to break a grip, setting up the next strike.
jappyosul.name: Jappyosul tae

giokja.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Joong-Gun. The fist travels across the body to the opposite side at chin height, the arm bent like the letter ㄱ. Done slowly.
giokja.name: Giokja jirugi

digutja.desc: An ITF block, first met in Joong-Gun. Both arms block at once, one forearm at head height and the other at middle height, the hands forming a ㄷ (U) shape as if catching a pole.
digutja.name: Digutja makgi

anpalmokm.desc: An ITF block, first met in Toi-Gye: the inner forearm blocks to the front at shoulder height, the forearm upright, here done in L-stance.
anpalmokm.name: Anpalmok kaunde makgi

yopdwi.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Toi-Gye. Standing feet together, the back fist swings back past the shoulder to strike behind at head height while the other arm extends down to the side. Done slowly.
yopdwi.name: Dung joomuk yopdwi taerigi

twinelbow.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Toi-Gye. Standing feet together, both elbows thrust out to the sides at once, fists in front of the chest. Done slowly.
twinelbow.name: Sang yop palkup tulgi

doolowpush.desc: An ITF block, first met in Toi-Gye. In L-stance the front forearm pushes down and forward at low height, the other fist bracing it.
doolowpush.name: Doo palmok najunde miro makgi

grabhead.desc: An ITF movement in Toi-Gye: both hands reach up as if to take hold of the opponent's head, slipping forward into walking stance, then pull it down onto the rising knee.
grabhead.name: Japgi

yopdwilow.desc: An ITF combination in Toi-Gye: in L-stance, one back fist strikes behind at head height while the other forearm blocks low to the front, both at once.
yopdwilow.name: Dung joomuk yopdwi taerigi · palmok najunde makgi
yopdwilow.ko: 등주먹 옆뒤 때리기 · 팔목 낮은데 막기
yopdwilow.en: Back fist side back strike with low block

itf.name: Dung joomuk yopdwi taerigi · palmok najunde makgi
itf.ko: 등주먹 옆뒤 때리기 · 팔목 낮은데 막기
itf.en: Back fist side back strike with low block

kslowguard.desc: An ITF block, first met in Toi-Gye. In L-stance the front knife-hand blocks low over the front knee while the rear knife-hand guards in front of the solar plexus.
kslowguard.name: Sonkal najunde daebi makgi

moajunbic.desc: An ITF ready posture, first met in Hwa-Rang. Feet together; the left hand wraps the right fist, held lower than in ready stance B, in front of the lower abdomen.
moajunbic.name: Moa junbi sogi C

yobapmiro.desc: An ITF block, first met in Hwa-Rang. The palm pushes across in front of the chest to move an attack aside, here in sitting stance.
yobapmiro.name: Sonbadak kaunde yobap miro makgi

ollyojirugi.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Hwa-Rang. The fist drives upward close in front of the body, palm toward you, while the other fist is pulled across in front of the opposite shoulder.
ollyojirugi.name: Ollyo jirugi

ksdown.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Hwa-Rang. The knife-hand comes down from above the shoulder in front of the body, the edge of the hand leading; done in vertical stance.
ksdown.name: Sonkal naeryo taerigi

sideprep.desc: The set-up for a side piercing kick in Hwa-Rang: the rear foot is drawn up to the front foot, the left palm rests on the right fist and the right elbow bends outward. The ITF text gives no Korean name for it; the one here is ours.
sideprep.name: Yopcha jirugi junbi

yopelbow.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Hwa-Rang. The elbow is driven straight back or out to the side, the fist close to the chest, often with a sliding step toward the target.
yopelbow.name: Yop palkup tulgi

anyobap.desc: An ITF block, first met in Hwa-Rang. Standing feet together, the inner forearm blocks to the front-side while the other forearm extends down to the side.
anyobap.name: Anpalmok yobap makgi

rdfront.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Choong-Moo. The reverse knife-hand (the thumb-side edge of the open hand) swings round to the front at head height, the other hand held under the striking elbow.
rdfront.name: Sonkal dung nopunde ap taerigi

flyskick.desc: An ITF kick, first met in Choong-Moo. A step, then a jump forward with a side piercing kick in the air, landing ready to block.
flyskick.name: Twimyo yopcha jirugi

bkick.desc: An ITF kick, first met in Choong-Moo. With the back to the target, the foot drives straight back, heel first, looking over the shoulder.
bkick.name: Dwitcha jirugi

apmakgi.desc: An ITF block, first met in Choong-Moo. The forearm comes up in front of the body, fist at shoulder height, to block toward the front; here in sitting stance before a back fist strike to the side.
apmakgi.name: Palmok kaunde ap makgi

ksxcheck.desc: An ITF block, first met in Choong-Moo. Both knife-hands cross at the wrists in front of the chest to stop an attack before it starts.
ksxcheck.name: Kyocha sonkal momchau makgi

sangollyo.desc: An ITF block, first met in Choong-Moo. Both palms rise together in front of the body to lift an attack upward.
sangollyo.name: Sang sonbadak ollyo makgi

haneulson.desc: An ITF ready posture, first met in Kwang-Gae. Feet parallel; both open hands are raised slowly in front of the forehead, thumbs and forefingers touching to make a triangle you look through toward the sky.
haneulson.name: Narani sogi haneul son
haneulson.en: Parallel stance with a heaven hand

itf.name: Narani sogi haneul son
itf.en: Parallel stance with a heaven hand

upsetpunch.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Kwang-Gae. The fist travels forward palm up, the elbow bent, striking at solar-plexus height.
upsetpunch.name: Dwijibo jirugi

golchohi.desc: An ITF block, first met in Kwang-Gae. As the palm middle hooking block, but at head height: the palm hooks an attack aside and holds it.
golchohi.name: Sonbadak nopunde golcho makgi

kshguard.desc: An ITF block, first met in Kwang-Gae. The knife-hand guarding block made at head height, the other hand guarding in front of the chest.
kshguard.name: Sonkal nopunde daebi makgi

kslowfront.desc: An ITF block, first met in Kwang-Gae. The knife-hand swings round in a circle and down in front of the body, slapping into the other palm.
kslowfront.name: Sonkal najunde ap makgi

pressingkick.desc: An ITF kick, first met in Kwang-Gae. The foot sweeps out and presses down with the foot sword at knee height, usually straight into a side piercing kick with the same leg.
pressingkick.name: Bakuro noollo chagi

doopalmokm.desc: An ITF block, first met in Kwang-Gae. The forearm blocks at middle height with the other fist bracing it under the elbow.
doopalmokm.name: Doo palmok kaunde makgi

waebaljunbi.desc: The set-up for the pressing kick in Po-Eun: stand on one leg facing D, both fists lifted, the face turned to the side you will kick.
waebaljunbi.name: Waebal sogi

presside.desc: An ITF combination, first met in Po-Eun. In sitting stance, one forefist presses down in front of the body while the other inner forearm blocks to the front-side, at the same time.
presside.name: Ap joomuk noollo makgi wa anpalmok yobap makgi
presside.en: Forefist pressing block with inner forearm side front block

itf.name: Ap joomuk noollo makgi wa anpalmok yobap makgi
itf.en: Forefist pressing block with inner forearm side front block

anwedge.desc: An ITF block, first met in Po-Eun. Both inner forearms spread apart at middle height to open an attack from the front.
anwedge.name: Anpalmok kaunde hechyo makgi

backelbow.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Po-Eun. The elbow drives straight back to a target behind, the other palm pushing on the fist to help it.
backelbow.name: Dwit palkup tulgi

soopyong.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Po-Eun. The fist punches straight out to the side at shoulder height, the arm level with the floor.
soopyong.name: Soopyong jirugi

xslowfront.desc: An ITF block, first met in Po-Eun. Stepping into X-stance, the outer forearm blocks low to the front while the fingers of the other hand rest on the blocking forearm.
xslowfront.name: Bakat palmok najunde ap makgi

ugrasp.desc: An ITF grab, first met in Po-Eun. Both hands open into a U shape, one above the other, to seize the opponent's neck or arm.
ugrasp.name: Digutja japgi

twinelbowh.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Po-Eun. Standing feet together, both arms fold level at shoulder height and the elbows thrust out to the sides, slowly, the face turned to one side.
twinelbowh.name: Sang palkup soopyong tulgi

rdlowguard.desc: An ITF block, first met in Po-Eun. A low guarding block made with the reverse knife-hand (the thumb-side edge), here to the side from sitting stance.
rdlowguard.name: Sonkal dung najunde daebi makgi

twistkick.desc: An ITF kick, first met in Ge-Baek. The knee rises across the body and the foot snaps out and upward on a slant, twisting the hip, to a low target.
twistkick.name: Najunde bituro chagi

doobandal.desc: An ITF block, first met in Ge-Baek. Both arc-hands rise above the forehead toward a diagonal, close together, and you look through the gap between them.
doobandal.name: Nopunde doo bandalson makgi

scoop.desc: An ITF block, first met in Ge-Baek. The palm scoops up under a kick from below to lift and catch it, usually straight before a punch.
scoop.name: Sonbadak duro makgi

bffront.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Ge-Baek. The back fist swings up and forward to strike straight ahead at head height.
bffront.name: Dung joomuk ap taerigi

gutja.desc: An ITF block, first met in Ge-Baek. One forearm blocks upward to the side, bent like the numeral 9, while the other fist sits under its elbow; done in sitting stance.
gutja.name: Gutja makgi

joongji.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Ge-Baek. A middle punch with the middle knuckle pushed forward from the fist, the other side fist drawn in front of the opposite shoulder.
joongji.name: Joongji joomuk kaunde jirugi

moajunbid.desc: An ITF ready posture, first met in Eui-Am. Feet together, the hands held together in front of the body; drawn here like the other close ready stances.
moajunbid.name: Moa junbi sogi D

kslowin.desc: An ITF block, first met in Eui-Am. The knife-hand sweeps inward and down to the centre line to turn a low attack aside.
kslowin.name: Sonkal najunde anuro makgi

xdown.desc: An ITF block, first met in Eui-Am. Both fists cross at the wrists and drive down in front of the body to stop a low attack.
xdown.name: Kyocha joomuk naeryo makgi

ksrising.desc: An ITF block, first met in Eui-Am. The knife-hand rises above the forehead, edge up, to lift an attack from above.
ksrising.name: Sonkal chookyo makgi

revturn.desc: An ITF kick, first met in Eui-Am. The leg swings out and round the opposite way to a turning kick, hooking the target with the heel or the back of the foot.
revturn.name: Bandae dollyo chagi

crescentpunch.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Eui-Am. The fist travels in a crescent, curving in from the side to strike at head height.
crescentpunch.name: Nopunde bandal jirugi

turnpunch.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Eui-Am. The fist swings round horizontally to strike the side of the body, done slowly while drawing into parallel stance.
turnpunch.name: Kaunde dollyo jirugi

kswedge.desc: An ITF block, first met in Eui-Am. Both knife-hands spread apart from the centre at middle height to open a two-handed attack.
kswedge.name: Sonkal kaunde hechyo makgi

rdcircular.desc: An ITF block, first met in Eui-Am. The reverse knife-hand sweeps round in a circle toward a diagonal to carry an attack away.
rdcircular.name: Sonkal dung dollimyo makgi

altpalm.desc: An ITF block, first met in Eui-Am. Both palms press down together, one a little ahead of and lower than the other, as you pull back into rear foot stance.
altpalm.name: Euhkallin sonbadak naeryo makgi

rdlowin.desc: An ITF block, first met in Eui-Am. The reverse knife-hand sweeps inward and down to the centre line, usually while shifting back.
rdlowin.name: Sonkal dung najunde anuro makgi

doublefinger.desc: An ITF thrust, first met in Choong-Jang. The forefinger and middle finger, spread apart, thrust at the eyes.
doublefinger.name: Doo songarak nopunde tulgi

groundkick.desc: In Choong-Jang: dropping onto the left knee with both hands on the floor, the right leg swings round in a high turning kick.
groundkick.name: Nopunde dollyo chagi
groundkick.en: High turning kick from the ground

itf.name: Nopunde dollyo chagi
itf.en: High turning kick from the ground

groundpunch.desc: In Choong-Jang: still low after the turning kick from the ground, a high punch with one fist while the other palm presses on the floor.
groundpunch.name: Joomuk nopunde jirugi

kneelowkick.desc: In Choong-Jang: a low kick forward with the knee while both hands pull in, as if catching the opponent's leg. The texts call it a low front snap kick with the knee.
kneelowkick.name: Moorup najunde apcha busigi
kneelowkick.en: Low front kick with the knee

itf.name: Moorup najunde apcha busigi
itf.en: Low front kick with the knee

twinpress.desc: An ITF block, first met in Choong-Jang. Both palms press down together in front of the body.
twinpress.name: Sang sonbadak noollo makgi

houterfront.desc: An ITF block, first met in Choong-Jang. The outer forearm blocks in front of the face, straight ahead, before a back fist strike.
houterfront.name: Bakat palmok nopunde ap makgi

backhanddown.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Choong-Jang. The back of the open hand swings down in front of the body, with a stamp.
backhanddown.name: Sondung naeryo taerigi

palmpunch.desc: In Choong-Jang: straight after the back hand strike, the other fist punches into the open palm, which stays where it struck.
palmpunch.name: Kaunde baro jirugi

bfsidefront.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Choong-Jang. The back fist strikes to the front-side at head height while the elbow of the same arm hits the other open palm.
bfsidefront.name: Dung joomuk nopunde yobap taerigi
bfsidefront.en: Back fist high side front strike

itf.name: Dung joomuk nopunde yobap taerigi
itf.en: Back fist high side front strike

twinkshoriz.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Choong-Jang. Both knife-hands swing round level at neck height, one from each side.
twinkshoriz.name: Sang sonkal soopyong taerigi

archigh.desc: An ITF strike, first met in Choong-Jang. The arc-hand (between thumb and forefinger) drives forward at the throat or jaw.
archigh.name: Bandal son nopunde taerigi

twinknuckle.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Choong-Jang. Both fists, the forefinger knuckle pushed out, curve in together toward the temples.
twinknuckle.name: Sang inji joomuk nopunde bandal jirugi
twinknuckle.en: Twin fore-knuckle fist high crescent punch

itf.name: Sang inji joomuk nopunde bandal jirugi
itf.en: Twin fore-knuckle fist high crescent punch

openfist.desc: An ITF punch, first met in Choong-Jang. A high punch with the open fist: the fingers bent at the middle joints, striking with the second knuckles.
openfist.name: Pyon joomuk nopunde jirugi

tgrab.name: Sonnal eopeo japgi
tgrab.desc: The open hand twists over and grabs the opponent's wrist, ready to pull them onto the next strike.

kneebreak.name: Mureup kkeokgi
kneebreak.desc: One hand holds the opponent's kicking foot at the waist while the other hand presses down hard on the knee.

kick.name: Ap chagi
kick.desc: The knee lifts first, then the lower leg snaps straight out and back, striking with the ball of the foot. In the forms it comes from the rear leg, and you land a step forward.

jkick.name: Twimyeo ap chagi
jkick.desc: A front kick made in the air: the first leg lifts as a feint, the second kicks high at the top of the jump.

dskick.name: Geodeup yeop chagi
dskick.desc: Two side kicks from the same leg without setting the foot down: first low to the knee, then high.

skick.name: Yeop chagi
skick.desc: The knee lifts across the body, then the leg drives straight out to the side, striking with the foot blade. The body leans away and the supporting foot turns.

bskick.name: Dwi dora yeop chagi
bskick.desc: The body spins round backwards and the rear leg shoots out in a side kick in the direction you were travelling, striking with the foot blade.

hskick.name: Yeop chagi · mejumeok bakkat chigi
hskick.desc: A side kick with a hammer-fist strike out the same side at the same moment, the arm and leg extending together.

rkick.name: Dollyeo chagi
rkick.desc: The knee lifts and the hips turn over so the lower leg swings round horizontally to the target.

tkick.name: Pyojeok chagi
tkick.desc: A crescent kick that swings inward into your own open palm, held out as a target.

knee.name: Mureup chigi
knee.desc: Both hands grab and pull the opponent's head down while the knee drives straight up.
